metadata.title: गोवर्धन पूजा २०२४ : अन्नकूट का भोग, मुखर्जी नगर, दिल्ली
metadata.description:
Govardhan Puja, also called Annakut or Annakoot, is a special festival celebrated by Hindus to worship Lord Krishna. It holds great importance because it reminds everyone of the story where Lord Krishna lifted the Govardhan Hill to protect the villagers of Vrindavan from heavy rain sent by Lord Indra. On this day, people pray, sing devotional songs, and perform rituals to show their love and gratitude to Krishna, asking for his blessings and protection.  

In Mathura, where the Govardhan Hill is located, people celebrate the festival by walking around the hill in a ritual called Govardhan Parikrama. Those who cannot visit the hill make a small image of Krishna lifting the Govardhan Hill using cow dung at home. 

This year, we celebrated Govardhan Puja at the Shiv Mandir in Mukherjee Nagar. We participated in the rituals, listened to the chief priest explained the significance of the festival and the story of Lord Krishna lifting the Govardhan Hill to protect the people of Vrindavan. The atmosphere was filled with devotion as prayers and hymns were recited. After the puja, we partook in the Annakut Prasad, a special offering made of a variety of delicious dishes symbolizing abundance and gratitude. It was a spiritually enriching experience.
